name: Westinghouse iGen4500
summary: A 3,700-running-watt inverter with remote start and an 18-hour tank, sized for a fridge, freezer, sump pump and furnace in an outage without an open-frame engine's noise.
verdict:
The iGen4500 is the quiet mid-size inverter to buy when a 2,200-watt suitcase unit is too small for your outage list. Westinghouse rates it at 3,700 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 4,500 peak watts from a 224cc engine, with clean output rated under 3 percent [THD](/glossary/thd/).

**Size it to your loads.** A modern refrigerator runs at about 150 to 200 watts, a chest freezer about 100, a 1/2 HP sump pump about 800 to 1,000 and a gas furnace blower about 500 to 800. Together that is near 2,000 running watts, well inside 3,700, with room for the surge when a compressor kicks on. Stagger the starts and you can add lights, internet and a TV. Run your own list through the [generator wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/).

**The run time is the point.** The 3.4-gallon tank is rated for up to 18 hours at a quarter load (one Westinghouse sheet lists 16), so one fill can carry a typical overnight essentials load. Noise is rated as low as 52 dBA at light load.

**Know the limits.** It is 120V only, with a 5-20R duplex, a [TT-30R](/glossary/tt-30/) RV outlet and two USB ports, so it cannot run a 240V well pump or feed a split-phase panel. It weighs close to 100 lb, depending on the sheet, so you will use the wheels. Westinghouse's site now shows the gas-only iGen5000 (3,900 running watts) where this model used to be, so check which one a listing sells.

Owners praise the remote start fob and the display that shows load and fuel left; the main complaint is the weight. It features in our [best inverter generator](/best-inverter-generator/) and [best small generator for home](/best-small-generator-for-home/) roundups.

name: Honda EU2200i
summary: Honda's 1,800-running-watt suitcase inverter: quiet, 47 lb and famously reliable, the default for a fridge, lights and internet at home or a campsite.
verdict:
The EU2200i is the small inverter the rest of the class is measured against. Honda rates it at 1,800 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 2,200 starting watts from its 121cc GXR120 engine, at 47.4 lb dry.

**Size it to the essentials.** 1,800 watts covers a refrigerator (about 150 to 200 running watts), a modem and router (about 20), a few LED lights, a TV and phone charging, with room for a gas furnace blower while the fridge is cycling. It will not run a window AC and a fridge together, a space heater with much else, or anything 240V. Check your list with the [generator wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/).

**Fuel math.** Honda lists 3.2 hours at rated load and 8.1 hours at a quarter load on the 0.95-gallon tank. A fridge-plus-lights load sits near a quarter load, so plan on refilling about three times a day, roughly 3 gallons, in a long outage.

**Quiet enough for close neighbors.** Honda rates it at 48 dBA at a quarter load and 57 dBA at rated load. CO-MINDER shuts the engine down if carbon monoxide builds up around it, and a second unit can be added with a parallel kit when you need more.

Owners report reliable starts after years of seasonal use and dealer support almost everywhere; the main complaint is price compared with the [Champion 2500W Ultralight](/gear/champion-2500-inverter/). It features in our [best inverter generator](/best-inverter-generator/), [best generator for camping](/best-generator-for-camping/) and [best small generator for home](/best-small-generator-for-home/) roundups.

name: Champion 2500W Ultralight Inverter
summary: Champion's 39 lb, 1,850-running-watt inverter with CO Shield and parallel ports, the budget alternative to a Honda EU2200i for camping and fridge-and-lights outages.
verdict:
The Champion 2500W Ultralight is the value pick among small inverters: most of a Honda EU2200i's job for a fraction of the price. Champion rates it at 1,850 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 2,500 [starting watts](/glossary/starting-watts/) from a 79cc engine, at about 39 lb.

**More surge than the Honda.** Its 2,500 starting watts beat the EU2200i's 2,200, which helps when a refrigerator compressor or a small pump kicks on while other loads are running. Running output is 50 watts higher too. Keep the steady load under about 1,500 watts and it handles a fridge, lights, internet, a TV and a CPAP together.

**Fuel and noise.** Champion lists up to 11.5 hours at a quarter load on the 1.05-gallon tank, so an overnight fridge-and-lights load is realistic on one fill. The 53 dBA rating is measured at 23 feet, one of the few figures in the class with a stated distance.

**Safety and growth.** CO Shield shuts the engine off if carbon monoxide builds up, a backstop for, not a substitute for, placing it at least 20 feet from the house. A [parallel kit](/glossary/parallel-kit/) links it to a second Champion inverter for about 3,700 running watts combined.

Owners describe it as easy to start and easy to carry; the main complaint is that Champion's long-term engine record is shorter than Honda's or Yamaha's. Compare it with the [Honda EU2200i](/gear/honda-eu2200i/) and see our [best inverter generator](/best-inverter-generator/) and [best small generator for home](/best-small-generator-for-home/) roundups.

name: Generac GP3500iO

summary: An open-frame inverter with 3,000 running watts, PowerRUSH motor starting and an 11-hour tank, the most watts per dollar for a home essentials load if noise is not critical.
verdict:
The GP3500iO gives you the most running watts per dollar among these inverters, as long as you can live with an open frame. Generac rates it at 3,000 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 3,500 starting watts from a 212cc engine, at 74.3 lb.

**PowerRUSH helps with motors.** Generac says PowerRUSH adds starting capacity for motor loads, so a sump pump, a window AC or a fridge compressor is more likely to start without tripping the overload. That makes a refrigerator (about 200 running watts), a chest freezer (about 100), a 1/2 HP sump pump (about 1,000) and lights a realistic combined load, if the motors start one at a time.

**Strong run time for the size.** The 2.37-gallon tank is rated for 8 hours at half load and 11 at a quarter load, so a typical outage load gets through the night on one fill.

**The open frame is the trade.** Without an enclosure, more engine noise escapes, so it suits a backyard better than a narrow side yard by a neighbor's window. Outlets are a 5-20R duplex, a 30-amp L5-30R twist-lock and two USB ports; an RV with a [TT-30](/glossary/tt-30/) plug needs an adapter. COsense shuts the engine off if carbon monoxide builds up, and a [parallel kit](/glossary/parallel-kit/) pairs it with another Generac 3300 or 3500-series inverter.

Owners like the price and easy starts; the main complaint is noise compared with enclosed units like the [Westinghouse iGen4500](/gear/westinghouse-igen4500/). summary: A low-cost 1,700-running-watt inverter with a 30-amp twist-lock, TT-30R adapter and built-in parallel ports, for a fridge and internet or a small trailer on a tight budget.
verdict:
The Firman W01784 is the cheapest real inverter in this group, and its spec sheet is better than the price suggests. Firman rates it at 1,700 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 2,100 starting watts from an 80cc engine, at 45.9 lb.

**Size it for one big load.** 1,700 watts runs a refrigerator (about 150 to 200 watts) plus internet, lights, a TV and phone charging, or a 1,500-watt space heater by itself. It will not run a fridge, a microwave and a coffee maker at once. Total your loads with the [generator wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/) and keep the sum under about 1,400 watts for margin.

**RV-ready for a small unit.** The panel has a 5-20R outlet, a 30-amp L5-30R twist-lock and a USB port, and Firman includes an L5-30P to [TT-30R](/glossary/tt-30/) adapter, so a small trailer can plug in. Output is rated under 3 percent THD, safe for laptops and furnace control boards.

**Fuel and noise.** Firman lists up to 10 hours at a quarter load on the 0.9-gallon tank, and 54 dBA at 7 meters at a quarter load. Parallel ports are built in, and the warranty is three years.

The trade-offs: Firman's spec sheet lists no carbon monoxide shutoff, so outdoor placement and a CO alarm inside matter even more, and the dealer network is thinner than Honda's or Champion's. Owners like the price and light weight. It features in our [best small generator for home](/best-small-generator-for-home/) roundup; the [Champion 2500W Ultralight](/gear/champion-2500-inverter/) adds CO Shield for a little more.

name: Honda EU7000iS
summary: Honda's fuel-injected 5,500-running-watt inverter with a 120/240V L14-30R outlet, the quiet way to back up a well pump and house circuits through a transfer switch.
verdict:
The EU7000iS is the rare inverter generator that makes 240 volts, which is why it is the pick for a quiet well-pump or panel backup. Honda rates it at 5,500 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 7,000 starting watts from a fuel-injected 389cc GX390 engine.

**240V is the point.** Most inverters are 120V only. This one has an [L14-30R](/glossary/l14-30/) 120/240V outlet, so an electrician can connect it through a [power inlet box](/glossary/power-inlet-box/) to a [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) or interlock kit and run 240V circuits. A 1/2 or 3/4 HP well pump is well within its range. A 1 HP pump can need roughly 3,000 to 4,000 watts or more to start, so let it start with other motor loads off and check your pump maker's sizing table.

**Long, quiet run time.** The 5.1-gallon tank is rated for 6.4 hours at rated load and 16 hours at a quarter load. Noise is rated at 52 dBA at a quarter load and 58 dBA at rated load, far quieter than a 7,000-watt open frame.

**Weight and price.** It weighs 263.2 lb dry, so it stays on its wheels, and it costs far more per watt than an open frame or the [Champion 201417](/gear/champion-201417/), which offers 9,000 running watts and dual fuel. You are paying for low noise, clean output, CO-MINDER shutoff and Honda's service network.

Owners praise how quietly it carries a house's essentials for days; the main complaint is price. See our [best generator for well pump](/best-generator-for-well-pump/) roundup and size your loads with the generator wattage calculator.

name: Yamaha EF2200iS
summary: Yamaha's 1,800-running-watt rival to the Honda EU2200i, with a longer 10.5-hour tank, a fuel gauge and a TT-30R outlet that suits camping and small RVs.
verdict:

Use the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) to size that pairing.

It is expensive per watt, has a single 15A duplex and no parallel capability, and you will outgrow it if you buy a trailer. Owners praise the weight and quiet idle; the main complaint is the short run time. faqs.a: Not on its own for most rooftop units. A 13,500 BTU AC needs about 2,500 to 3,000 watts to start, at or above the 2,550 peak rating, then 1,200 to 1,500 to run. Two iGen2550s in parallel, or one with a soft starter on a small AC, are the practical answers.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Westinghouse iGen2550 and the iGen2200?
faqs.a: The iGen2550 adds a TT-30R RV outlet, 350 more peak watts (2,550 vs 2,200) and 100 more running watts (1,900 vs 1,800). It is also about 3 lb lighter (43.2 vs 46.3 lb). The iGen2200 runs a little longer at quarter load, 12 hours against 11.

name: Westinghouse iGen2200
summary: Westinghouse's budget 1,800-running-watt inverter with a 12-hour quarter-load tank and 52 dBA rating, a low-cost stand-in for a Honda EU2200i for camping and essentials.
verdict:
The iGen2200 is the low-cost way to get Honda EU2200i output with a longer run time. Westinghouse rates it at 1,800 [running watts](/glossary/running-watts/) and 2,200 peak watts from an 80cc engine, at 46.3 lb dry, the same output class as the [Honda EU2200i](/gear/honda-eu2200i/).

**Run time beats the Honda.** The 1.14-gallon tank is rated for up to 12 hours at a quarter load, about 450 watts, against 8.1 hours for the EU2200i. A fridge, LED lights, a modem and phone charging sit near that load, so one fill can get you through the night in an outage.

**What 1,800 watts runs.** Add a TV, a CPAP or a laptop and you are still well inside the rating. A 1,500-watt kettle, hot plate or space heater runs on its own, not with much else. Total your loads with the [generator wattage calculator](/tools/generator-wattage-calculator/).

**Simple panel.** It has a 5-20R duplex and two USB ports, with no RV outlet; the [iGen2550](/gear/westinghouse-igen2550/) adds a [TT-30R](/glossary/tt-30/). Noise is rated at 52 dBA, and it can be paired with a second unit using a parallel kit when you need more.

The trade-offs: no CO sensor on this model, recoil start only, and Westinghouse's dealer network is smaller than Honda's, though the residential warranty is three years. Owners mostly praise the price and run time; the gaps to weigh are the missing CO sensor and the recoil start. faqs.q: How long will the Westinghouse iGen2200 run a refrigerator?
faqs.a: Up to about 12 hours per tank. A fridge plus a few lights and a modem averages roughly 300 to 450 watts, near the quarter-load point where Westinghouse rates 12 hours on the 1.14-gallon tank. Plan on about 2.5 gallons of gasoline for a 24-hour outage at that load.

faqs.q: Is the Westinghouse iGen2200 safe to run indoors?
faqs.a: No. It has no CO sensor, and no gasoline generator is safe indoors, in a garage or under a carport, even with doors open. Run it at least 20 feet from the house with the exhaust pointed away from windows, and keep battery-powered CO alarms inside.
